function: Assignment of topological interference-alignment precoding ('beamforming') vectors to messages, via local graph coloring on message conflict graphs, for partially connected K-user interference channels (pp. 1-2, 7).
system: K-user partially connected interference channel (e.g., D2D pairs) with topology-only CSIT; SISO and SIMO-(1,N), N=2-3 receive antennas; no RIS; Wireless Net at 2.4 GHz (pp. 2, 6-7, 13).
method: Graph reinforcement learning (learning to defer): actor-critic with 4-layer GraphSAGE/GCN policy and value networks, trained with PPO and Adam (reinforcement learning) (pp. 8-9, 13).
data_channel: Synthetic Erdős-Rényi message-conflict graphs and Wireless Net D2D topologies whose links follow the ITU-R P.1411 LoS model; 50,000 training and 5,000 evaluation graphs (pp. 10, 13).
test_conditions: Training graphs grouped by chromatic number; Table I tests on same distribution; Table II trains on ER graphs of one size (15-30 nodes), tests on other sizes (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned graph-coloring heuristics SLI (smallest-last greedy with interchange) and TabuCol; MAIS outer bound for DoF; no learned baseline, stated as unavailable (p. 11).
metrics: Achievable symmetric DoF and share of instances meeting the MAIS bound, per IA scheme; optimal coloring ratio; running time in seconds (pp. 10-12).
complexity: Measured running times in seconds (Table I: 1.79-13.2 s for LCG); about 0.2 s per coding scheme on an RTX 4060 GPU; no complexity order (pp. 7, 12).
q1_support: p. 13: "the simulated channel follows the LoS model in ITU-1411", used only as path loss to set link topology; the other dataset is synthetic Erdős-Rényi graphs (p. 10). No 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channels.
q2_support: p. 12: "we train the LCG model on ER graphs of certain sizes and test its generalization ability exclusively on ER graphs of different sizes" (Table II), i.e., other numbers of user pairs.
q3_support: p. 11: "there are no appropriate baselines available for comparison"; only "two heuristic algorithms: the smallest-last greedy method with interchange (SLI) [42], [43] and TabuCol [44]" are compared. No learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 12, Table I: "Running times (in seconds) are provided in brackets"; p. 7: "it only takes the LCG framework approximately 0.2 seconds to produce each coding scheme with an RTX 4060 GPU".
q5_support: p. 10, footnote 3: "The detailed experiment setups and implementation are available at https://github.com/ZhiweiShan/Learning-to-Code-on-Graphs".
notes: Area 3 is a judgment call for the reviewer: the learned GNN and RL framework assigns IA precoding ('beamforming') vectors over channel uses for topological interference management; transmitters are single-antenna and receivers have 1 to 3 antennas, so it is transmit precoder design rather than BS spatial beamforming, and its 'coding' is linear IA precoding, not channel coding (pp. 2-3, 7). Under a strict reading of area 3 the reason would be 'function'. The system check passes because SIMO-(1,2) and SIMO-(1,3) receivers are evaluated (pp. 7, 11). q1: the Wireless Net topologies use the ITU-R P.1411 LoS model (p. 13), a standardized ITU model, but only its path loss sets connectivity and most results use synthetic ER graphs, so I marked 0 by analogy with the 3GPP path-loss rule; the reviewer may count it as another standardized model. Performance metrics are symmetric DoF and graph-coloring optimal ratio, not rate.
